comments.author: Russell Powell
comments.text:
Update: Misdiagnosis Corrected

Original assumption: Embedded Dolt missing depends_on_id column prevented bd close and bd dep add.

Actual cause: Beads application-level validation rule:
- Epics can only block other epics (not tasks)
- Tasks can only block other tasks (not epics)
- Parent/child (containment) is separate from depends_on (blocking)

Evidence:
- bd close operations succeed without error
- bd dep add succeeds when using task→task blocking
- Dolt database schema is healthy; depends_on_id column exists and works

Correct pattern:
- Use bd update --parent for epic→task containment
- Use bd dep add for task→task blocking dependencies

Action: This bead (web-rb7) can be closed or updated as the schema error does not exist. The constraint is behavioral, not structural.

Related refinement: Successfully created full dependency graph for epic web-e7r using proper parent+depends_on relationships.

title: Infinite loop when auto-searching HF metadata for models without repo
description:
When a model with no Hugging Face repository is selected, the panel automatically triggers a search (as designed). However, this causes an infinite loop:

1. selectModel() → renderPanelProperties()
2. renderPanelProperties() auto-clicks the 'Find on Hugging Face' button (when repo is missing)
3. Click handler calls updateModelRepo()
4. updateModelRepo() calls selectModel() again to refresh
5. repeat from step 1, causing flashing and continuous rebuilding

Root cause: The auto-click in renderPanelProperties() creates a re-entrant call to selectModel() before the model data actually updates. The stale data still shows no repo, triggering auto-click again.

Fix approach: Remove the auto-click behavior. The manual 'Find on Hugging Face' button is sufficient.

Acceptance criteria:
- No infinite loop when selecting models without repo
- Panel remains stable; manual button works to search and select repo

description:

title: Fix missing progress bar in re-download flow
description:
Problem: When a model is re-downloaded using the resume functionality (downloadWithResume), the progress bar does not appear.

Root cause: downloadWithResume initializes state and starts the SSE progress listener, but does not inject the progress bar HTML into the tile DOM. The initial download flow includes progress bar HTML during tile rendering, but programmatic downloads bypass that render pass.

Required fix in templates/index.html:
- In downloadWithResume, before calling startProgressListener(model):
  1. Compute safeId from model name (same logic as showProgressBar)
  2. Find the tile element matching data-model attribute
  3. Construct progress bar HTML with IDs: progress-, progress-bar-, progress-text-
  4. Append the progress bar container to the tile
  5. Then start the listener

Expected structure:
- Container: div with class 'progress-container' and id progress-
- Bar: div with class 'progress-bar' and id progress-bar- (width set by JS)
- Text: span with class 'progress-text' and id progress-text-

Validation: After fix, re-download should show progress bar identical to initial download.

title: Fix re-download button to use direct model-file endpoint
description:
The re-download button (and download button) in the model grid currently uses , which performs a HuggingFace filename-based search that fails due to normalization mismatches. Root cause: The filename search relies on extracting a base name and matching filenames from search results, which is brittle and unnecessary since we already store the exact repo and filename in models.json. The original add-model flow uses direct URL construction without search.

title: Progress bar auto-update during download
description:
The model tile download progress bar does not automatically update as the file downloads. It only refreshes when manually clicking the refresh button.

Root cause: The SSE listener (startProgressListener) updates the downloadProgressState but does not update the DOM. The progress bar is only rendered (or updated) during refresh() calls, and there is no periodic refresh during a download. SSE updates therefore become invisible until the user manually triggers a refresh.

Fix: Modify startProgressListener() to directly update the progress bar DOM elements on each SSE message after updating downloadProgressState. This will make the progress bar reflect real-time progress without requiring a full UI refresh.
